 Dated this the 7th day of August 2025

Petitioners: 1. Smt.Parvathi Bai, 67 years,
 W/o Chandrappa
 2. Sri.Rajesh C Patil , 48 years,
 S/o Chandrappa,
 Both are residing at; No.26,
 1st cross, Telecom Layout,

(By Sri.T.S.,Advocate)
 /Vs/

Respondents: 1.M/s Suryawanshi Enterprises  Thamane Nagar Gar,
 No87/P/6/P/16, Akluj Bus Stand,
 Taj Malshiras, Solapur,
 Maharasthra - 413101  (owner of the Electric Car bearing  No.KA-03-AL-9506)

2. TATA AIG GIC Ltd.,
 No.69, JP & Devi, Jambukeshwara Arcade  3rd Floor, Millers Road  Bangalore - 52  (Policy No.0148024700  Valid from 01.02.2024 to 31.01.2025 )
 (R1-Sri.RS, Advocate  R2- Sri.NR, advocate)
 2 MVC No.5353/2024  JUDGMENT Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.
2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the son of Late Chandrappa.

Parvathi Bai vs Suryawanshi Enterprises on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70282221/
1

That on 19.04.2024 at 02.15 pm, Chandrappa S/o Mallappa was riding the TVS XL bearing Reg No.KA-50-R- 4762 in MCECHS Layout main road, near Hennur petrol bunk, wherein the driver of the Electric Car bearing Reg No.KA-03-AL-9506, drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident, in the accident Chandrappa sustained grievous injuries and he was shifted to Regal Hospital, wherein first aid was done and later he was shifted to Suraksha Hospital and further he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bangalore,

Further on 24.04.2024 he died due to the accidental injuries, that is on the way,
while he was shifting to the other hospital.
Autopsy was conducted at Dr.B.R.Ambedkar Medical College & Hospital, Bangalore.
Petitioners have performed the funeral and obsequies as per their customs and they have spent more than Rs.7,50,000/- for the same.

3. Petitioners alleged that Late.Chandrappa was aged about 76 yeas of age as on the date of the accident and prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was running private Tutorials and thereby he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

They alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.44/2024.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent No.1 is the of the owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent No.2 is the insurer, accordingly they are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, Respondents have appeared through their counsel.
Counsel for respondent No.1 filed memo of appearance on 19.09.2024 and he has not chosen to file written statement.

Respondent No.2 filed the written statement contending that insured has violated the policy conditions and late Chandrappa was not having valid driving license and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. In order to prove the case, the Petitioner No.2 examined himself as PW-1, produced and marked 14 documents which are at Ex.P-1 to 14 and he is fully cross examined.

Respondent No.2 has not chosen to lead the evidence and there is no material on record to show that respondent No.2 is prevented from leading the evidence accordingly evidence of respondent No.2 is taken as Nil.
6. I have heard the arguments from the counsels appearing for both the sides and perused the entire records.

7. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed follows:
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioners prove that on 19.04.2024 at 2.15 pm, Chandrappa, S/o.
Parvathi Bai vs Suryawanshi Enterprises on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70282221/
2

Mallappa was driving the vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-50-R-4762, in MCECHS Layout main road,
Bengaluru, wherein the driver of Electric Car beg. No. KA-03-AL-9506 drove it with high speed,
rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident, in the accident Chandrappa sustained grievous injuries and he died due to the accidental injuries as alleged in the petition.?
2.Whether respondent no.2 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions and the two wheeler was unfit for use and Chandrappa was not having valid DL as consented in the written statement.?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
4.
What order
or award?

8. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue no.2: In the Negative  Issue no.3: In Partly Affirmative  Issue No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 9. Issues No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner no.2 and the son of Late Chandrappa, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.
10. According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle that is Shivu S/o Hanumanthappa, Doddallari.

In order to prove the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioners have tendered the FIR,
complaint, mahazar, sketch, Inquest report, PM report, 133 Notice & reply notice and final report which are at Ex.P1 to 8, & 11.
11.
On perusal and analysis of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that deceased Chandrappa died due to the accidental injuries.
Ex.P.11 is the final report filed after fair investigation and it is not disputed by the respondent.

It is true that Shivu S/o Hanumanthappa was the driver of the offending vehicle and as per the reply notice given by the respondent No.1, Shivu was having valid driving license and insurance policy of the offending vehicle was in force as on the date of the accident.

The final report, inquest, PM report, death intimation, death summary,
mahazar, sketch which are at Ex.P5, 6 and 10 to 12, 3, 4 establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and negligent act of its driver.
Further more, the aforesaid documents reveals that Chandrappa died due to the accidental injuries on 24.04.2024.

It is true that no allegation is made Parvathi Bai vs Suryawanshi Enterprises on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70282221/
3 against the Chandrappa and not chargsheet for any punishable offence in the final report.
In the cross examination of PW-1, he denied the suggestion that Chandrappa was unable to drive the two wheeler and vehicle was not insured and he was having no valid driving license.
Further final report is the prime facie proof for the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Respondent No.2 has failed to establish its contention as contended in the written statement.

12. Admittedly the accident occurred on 19.04.2024, petitioners have not substantiate the nature of work and the income of the deceased accordingly the notional income of Rs.16,500/- has to be considered as the income of the deceased as the accident occurred in the year 2024.
13. Further more as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.P.13, the date of birth of the deceased is 01.01.1948.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 76 years.
Accordingly the multiplier 5 is applicable.
14. Deceased was married and self employee and 76 years of age, accordingly future prospectus cannot be added to his monthly income.
Deceased has left behind 2 dependents accordingly 1/3 should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.

15. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1 Monthly income Rs.16,500/-
2 Less; 1/3 for personal expenses Rs.5,500 /- 4

Monthly income Rs.11,000/-
Rs.11,000 (income)X 12 (month) X 5 Rs.6,60,000/- (Multiplier ) Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.6,60,000/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.

16. Loss of estate;
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.

17 . Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.
18. Loss of Consortium :
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.
In the present case petitioners are the wife and son of the deceased and they are entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/- each.
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.80,000/- as compensation under this head.
Petitioners have tendered medical bills of Rs.5,78,106/- as per Ex.P.14 and they are entitled for the said amount.

Except the aforesaid compensation amount,
petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.

In total the petitioners are entitled for compensation as follows;

Compensation under the Head Amount 1 Loss of dependency Rs.6,60,000/-

2 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
3
Funeral expenses & transportation Rs. 15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium Rs. 80,000/-

5 Medical bills Rs.5,78,106/-
 TOTAL Rs.13,48,106/-
[S In total petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.13,48,106/-.
20. Rate of Interest:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s
Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
21. Liability:
The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle, Accordingly Respondent No.2 is the liable to pay the compensation amount with interest.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative, Issue No.2 in the negative and Issue No.3 in partly affirmative.
22. Issues No.4;
For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.13,48,106/- with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
Petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for 50% each, in the total compensation amount with interest

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioners are Parvathi Bai vs Suryawanshi Enterprises on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70282221/
5 permitted to withdraw their share of compensation amount with interest there on by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020, Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.
Any interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
